model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route): profit attributable to ordinary shareholders less CET1 retention, net debt zero, per ordinary share, GBP flows bridged to a GBp quote

equity_bridge.item: CET1 surplus above the c.13.0% target at 30 Jun 2026, plus the foreseeable buyback already deducted from CET1
equity_bridge.note: CET1 13.2% (H1-2026 :906) vs the c.13.0% target (:132): 0.2% x GBP 199.5bn RWA = GBP 399m. The 13.2% is after deducting GBP 1,517m of foreseeable ordinary dividends and a GBP 442m foreseeable charge for the share buyback (:1012-1014, :1023). The buyback cash is credited back (399 + 442 = 841) because its shares, including the 9.02m bought since 30 June, are not deducted from the share count. The foreseeable dividend is NOT credited: the 12.0p interim (about GBP 955m) has been paid and the price is ex-dividend; the remaining about GBP 560m accrual toward the final is left in the capital base, which is conservative by about 7p/share and matches the LLOY.L treatment.

Management expects Basel 3.1 to increase RWAs by around GBP 10 billion on 1 January 2027 (H1-2026 :136). Held at the 13.0% target that is GBP 1.3bn of one-off CET1 retention, deducted here rather than spread through the capex path.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (total income FY2022-FY2025, 13,156 to 16,641). Both revenue CAGRs are inflated by the 2022-25 rate cycle (NII 7,614 in FY2021 to 12,829 in FY2025) and are not a forward growth rate; the base path starts at 7.5% on FY26 guidance (income about GBP 17.9bn ex-notables, +7.6% on FY25, with Evelyn Partners and the GBP 1.5bn 2026 / GBP 1.0bn 2027 structural-hedge uplift) and fades to 2.5% GBP nominal by year 7.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (5.3% 3yr, -0.6% 5yr) diverges by more than 30% from the revenue CAGRs (8.1% / 9.0%) and the 3-year EPS CAGR (26.2%). NatWest distributes nearly all capital generation: about GBP 9.6bn of buybacks FY2021-25 (including the GBP 1.5bn directed buyback that completed the UK Government's exit in May 2025) cut ordinary shares in issue from 12,095m to 7,995m (-34%), so total equity is flat by design and is not a growth proxy. The 5-year EPS and attributable-profit CAGRs start at the FY2020 COVID-impairment loss (EPS -6.2p, attributable -753) and are undefined; the 3-year figures start at FY2022, the first full year of rising rates, and overstate the sustainable trend.
historical_growth.notes: 'FCF' here is the bank owner-flow proxy: profit attributable to ordinary shareholders (SBC is already a P&L expense). Reported FCF/OCF is not meaningful for a bank. No SBC-adjusted divergence exists, because SBC is about 1.4% of income. EPS is in GBP per ordinary share (CSV eps column); the GBp quote is not used in any CAGR.

scenario_narratives.base: NatWest delivers its raised 2026 guidance (income about GBP 17.9bn, RoTE >19%, capital generation >240bps ex-Evelyn) and holds RoTE around 20% for two years as the structural hedge reprices, then settles in the mid-to-high teens rather than sustaining the 2028 >18% target indefinitely. Impairment normalises from 19bps toward 30bps, deposit competition and lower base rates erode the hedge spread, and Evelyn Partners roughly breaks even in year 1 before contributing. CET1 is held at c.13% through Basel 3.1 (about GBP 10bn of RWA on 1 Jan 2027), with distributions of about 50% of earnings as dividends plus annual buybacks. Income growth fades to UK nominal GDP after the hedge tailwind is spent.
scenario_narratives.bull: A higher-for-longer UK curve and the hedge roll keep NII compounding beyond 2027. CAL grows above 4% a year as NatWest takes mortgage and SME share, C&I keeps lending at high single digits, and the enlarged wealth business (GBP 130bn AUMA) adds a capital-light fee line that is not rate-sensitive. Cost:income falls below 45% on the AI and platform programme, RoTE holds at about 20%, and the shares re-rate to above 2x TNAV with distributions running at 9-10% of market cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: A UK downturn arrives with faster rate cuts. Commercial and unsecured credit losses rise to about 60bps, deposit margins compress, Evelyn Partners disappoints, and a bank tax rise lands on top. Income falls 4% in year 2, buybacks pause for two years to rebuild CET1 through Basel 3.1, and RoTE settles around 13-14%. That is barely above the cost of equity, which at 1.79x reported TNAV leaves a long way to fall.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is worth what it can pay ordinary shareholders after funding the capital its growth requires. The flow is profit attributable to ordinary shareholders (after AT1 coupons and NCI) less the CET1 retention that holds the ratio at the c.13% target, discounted at a GBP cost of equity of 10.5%. Deposits are funding, not debt, so nothing is deducted for net debt. Value is therefore TNAV plus the PV of returns above the cost of equity. NatWest earns about 20% on tangible equity today, a 9-10pt spread over CoE, which the base case fades to about 16.5% by year 10 as the rate-cycle tailwind in NII normalises; that still justifies roughly 1.8-2.0x TNAV. The shares trade at 1.79x reported TNAV (359p at 30 June 2026) and about 8.6x TTM earnings, so the probability-weighted value sits modestly above the price: the return is the distribution yield (about 5% dividend plus buybacks) plus mid-single-digit growth, with a re-rating only if the 2028 targets are sustained. The LSE quote is in pence and the flows are in pounds, so a GBp holder carries no FX leg.
key_risks_to_valuation: UK rate cycle: NII is about 78% of income and the structural hedge smooths but does not remove sensitivity. FY26 guidance assumes a 3.75% base rate; faster BoE cuts plus deposit competition compress margins once the hedge uplift (GBP 1.5bn 2026, GBP 1.0bn 2027) is spent.

Credit: the base assumes impairment normalising to about 30bps from 19bps. A UK recession at about 60bps for a year costs about GBP 1.9bn pre-tax, and the C&I book (commercial real estate, SME, leveraged) is more cyclical than a mortgage book.
Valuation already at 1.79x TNAV: most of the value is the spread over CoE, so a 2pt lower terminal RoTE removes about 15% of IV, and a 50bp higher CoE about 7%.
Basel 3.1 (1 Jan 2027): about GBP 10bn of RWA, taken as GBP 1.3bn in the bridge; the final figure and any further PRA model changes could differ.
Evelyn Partners integration (GBP 2.2bn, completed 30 June 2026): client and adviser attrition or system-integration cost would make the first full year loss-making rather than breakeven.
UK bank tax and surcharge policy, and periodic industry-wide conduct and redress episodes (litigation and conduct GBP 167m in FY25), which the base carries only at the historical run-rate.

sanity_check_caveat.status: passed:true is a FALSE PASS - do not read the printed multiples
sanity_check_caveat.cause: scripts/sanity_check.py applies inputs.fx_rate quote->reporting while dcf_engine.py defines it model->quote (the documented systemic fx-direction bug, GBp form, same as HSBA.L and BT-A.L). With fx_rate = 100 it multiplies the pence price by 100 instead of dividing: the implied multiples are exactly 100x real (P/B 135.76 printed vs 1.36x; P/Sales 347.66 vs 3.48x) and the historical table is 10,000x (FY2019 price printed 25,878 vs the real about 259p; P/B 7,170 vs 0.72x). The verdict survives only because the inflated history inflates the thresholds by the same factor.
sanity_check_caveat.assessment: The implied 1.53x P/B at IV is above the FY2025 year-end 1.37x and far above the 2019-24 range (0.5-0.8x), but those years carried RoTE of -2% to 17.5% and a government overhang; at a 20% RoTE and 10.5% CoE a 1.5x book / 2.1x TNAV is the spread over CoE, not a multiple anomaly. No fix applied to the valuation. Recorded here rather than in scripts/ because the fix needs TDD and a corpus recompute per CLAUDE.md.
sanity_check_caveat.basis_ties_to: inputs.ordinary_shareholders_equity 38,748 / 7,959 shares in issue = 487p; TNAV 359p reported; TTM attributable 6,026 / 8,043 diluted = 74.9p EPS; TTM income 17,518.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted ordinary shares, millions, at 30 June 2026: 7,959m ordinary shares in issue excluding own shares (NWG.L_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:223, :4845) plus about 84m dilutive awards (H1-26 attributable profit 3,035 / diluted EPS 37.7p = 8,050m less 3,035 / basic EPS 38.1p = 7,966m, :3107-3108) = 8,043m. Per-share values are per ordinary share and match the LSE quote in pence. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flow and buybacks are value-neutral at IV. The 9.02m shares (GBP 59.6m) repurchased since 30 June (:4401) and the rest of the foreseeable buyback are not deducted from the count; the CET1 already set aside for them is credited in equity_bridge instead.
inputs.sbc_source: Share-based remuneration and shares vested under employee share schemes, CET1 capital flow statement: GBP 123m for H1-2026 (NWG.L_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:948), annualised to 246. The operating-expenses note (NWG.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:19007) describes the Sharesave, deferred performance, LTI and Sharing in Success plans but does not print a single group expense line. Awards are satisfied from shares, not net-settled for cash, so there is no equity-award tax line. SBC nets out of the bank flow because 'ebitda' adds it back and sbc_pct removes it; it only moves the street basis. reported_fcf = TTM profit attributable to ordinary shareholders 6,026 + SBC 246.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases GBP 579m on-market (KPI ShareRepurchases; a further GBP 1.5bn was the directed buyback from HM Treasury in May 2025 that completed the government exit, NWG.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:14518) plus ordinary dividends GBP 2,376m. H1-26: GBP 474m of buybacks (78.5m shares, H1-2026 :3265) and GBP 1,984m of dividends paid (final 21.5p). Interim dividend 12.0p (+26%, about GBP 955m), paid September 2026, so the 9 Oct price is ex-dividend. FY25 total DPS 32.5p (+51%). Management now expects to announce the next buyback with FY2026 results (:134-135). Ordinary shares in issue fell from 12,095m (FY2020) to 7,959m (H1-26), about GBP 9.6bn of buybacks FY2021-25.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows are GBP millions; the LSE quote is pence sterling. fx_rate converts model to quote: 1 GBP = 100 GBp, a fixed denomination bridge, not a market rate. The engine multiplies every GBP per-ordinary-share figure by it, so canonical intrinsic_value, weighted_iv and entry_price are in GBp and comparable to current_price; *_gbp siblings hold the model-currency figures. Parity check against the NYSE ADR (1 ADS = 2 ordinary shares), 2026-10-09 closes: NWG.L at inputs.price_as_of x 2 / 100 x GBPUSD 1.3233 (Yahoo GBPUSD=X, 2026-10-09T21:29Z) = US$17.01 per ADS-equivalent vs NWG ADS close US$17.13 (2026-10-09T20:00Z), 0.7% apart; the 2:1 ratio and the pence bridge hold. A GBp holder carries no FX translation risk.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T15:49:17Z regular close (LSE; Yahoo Finance chart API). Not an after-hours print.
inputs.tnav_note: Reported TNAV per ordinary share 359p at 30 June 2026, down from 384p at 31 Dec 2025: the Evelyn Partners acquisition (GBP 2.7bn of goodwill and intangibles) took 37p and the final dividend 20p (H1-2026 :306-308, :4848). Derived 28,891 / 7,959 = 363p; the Group's own TNAV definition takes a few further deductions. Price-to-TNAV commentary uses the reported 359p: the 9 Oct close is 1.79x.

Day-1 CET1 impact about 140bps (:308), of which GBP 2.7bn goodwill and intangibles. FY26 guidance includes about GBP 275m of income and GBP 300m of opex from Evelyn for H2-26, so year 1 carries it at roughly breakeven before synergies. Already in the 30 June balance sheet, share count and CET1; nothing further in the bridge.
inputs.anchor_sources: H1-2026 interim results (NWG.L_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt): three-column summary income statement H1-26 / H1-25 :160-179 (total income 8,862 / 7,985, opex 4,121 / 4,018, impairment 423 / 382, PBT 4,318 / 3,585, tax 1,138 / 910, attributable 3,035 / 2,488), paid-in equity holders (AT1) 149 / 186 and NCI (4) / 1 :3101-3102, CET1 13.2% / RWA 199,480 / CET1 capital 26,306 :906-917, CET1 reconciliation (shareholders' equity 43,818, other equity instruments 5,070, goodwill and intangibles 9,857, foreseeable dividends 1,517, foreseeable buyback 442) :995-1023, balance sheet equity (ordinary shareholders' interests 38,748, other owners' interests 5,070, NCI 10) :3180-3183, shares in issue 7,959m :223, TNAV 359p :4848, Basel 3.1 about +GBP 10bn RWA on 1 Jan 2027 :136, CET1 target around 13.0% :132. FY2025 annual report (NWG.L_Annual_FY2025.txt): FY25 income statement :5229-5365 (income 16,641, opex 8,262, impairment 671, PBT 7,708, tax 1,874, paid-in equity holders 352, NCI 3, attributable 5,479 :5774, :20194), ETR 24.3% :5362. H2-25 is FY25 less H1-25: income 8,656, opex 4,244, impairment 289, PBT 4,123, tax 964, AT1 166, NCI 2, attributable 2,991.
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP cost of equity of 10.5%, built in the currency of the flows. The 10-year gilt is about 4.6%, plus a beta of about 1.15 x 5.0% UK ERP = 10.35%, rounded up to 10.5%. Above LLOY.L / LYG (10.0%, a mortgage-led retail bank) because Commercial & Institutional is 53% of NatWest's income, with a commercial-credit book that is more cyclical than mortgages and a residual NatWest Markets trading business; below BCS (11.0%, about half investment bank) and level with HSBC / HSBA.L (10.5%). One rate across all three scenarios: risk is carried in the bear path and its weight, not in a per-scenario premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable. The bank FCFE flow is after all operating costs including premises and equipment (GBP 1,285m in FY25, which carries the IFRS 16 depreciation). Lease liabilities (GBP 535m at FY25, NWG.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:14999) are not debt in this model.
inputs.nci_treatment: Inside the flow. AT1 coupons (paid-in equity holders, GBP 315m TTM: H2-25 166 + H1-26 149) are deducted before the margin, so 'ebitda' = PBT + SBC - AT1 - NCI and the flow after tax is profit attributable to ordinary shareholders. NCI is negligible (GBP 10m of equity, -2m TTM share of profit, not grossed up). AT1 par (GBP 5,070m) is therefore NOT also deducted in the bridge (BCS/USB/WFC/HSBA.L/LLOY.L convention).
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, with net_debt = 0. SKILL.md routes banks to residual income on tangible book; the house precedent for large banks (BCS, HSBC, HSBA.L, NAB.AX, USB, WFC, LYG, LLOY.L) is FCFE-at-CoE on the engine route. That is the same economics (value = TNAV + PV of returns above CoE) expressed as distributable cash, and it keeps NWG.L comparable to LLOY.L, BCS and HSBA.L. Deposits (GBP 448.6bn) are operating funding, not debt. Subordinated liabilities (GBP 6.6bn, in kpis) and other financial liabilities / MREL are wholesale funding, not enterprise debt, so total_debt is deliberately 0. OCF is meaningless for a bank (the CSV swings from -43.6bn to +53.7bn). ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = statutory 'Total income'. TTM H2-25 + H1-26 = (16,641 - 7,985) + 8,862 = 17,518. 'ebitda' = PBT 8,441 + SBC 246 - AT1 315 + NCI 2 = 8,374 (47.8%). sbc_pct removes SBC, and D&A is 0 (inside operating costs). Cash tax: UK 25% corporation tax plus the 3% bank surcharge, but NatWest's reported ETR is 24.3% (FY25) / 26.4% (H1-26); on PBT after AT1 coupons the TTM rate is 2,102 / (8,441 - 315) = 25.9%, held at 26.0%. 'capex' = CET1 retention that holds CET1 at the c.13.0% target as RWA grows with income. Target CET1 = 13.0% x 199.5bn = 25.9bn, so CET1/revenue = 1.480 and capex% = 148.0 x g/(1+g). FY0 check: (8,374 - 246) x (1 - 25.9%) = 6,023, vs reported TTM attributable profit of 6,026. Notable items in TTM income (about GBP 190m in H1-26, :174) are left in; they are a small net positive and the year-1 margin is set from guidance, not from TTM. No one-off charge in FY0 needs normalising: litigation and conduct was GBP 167m in FY25 and GBP 45m in H1-26, and NatWest's motor-finance exposure is not material (no provision disclosed).

bear.margin_rationale: The BoE cuts faster into a UK slowdown (fiscal shock or consumer stress), compressing deposit margins below the hedge uplift, and unemployment overshoots the plan. Income falls 4% in year 2 and impairment reaches about 60bps (about GBP 2.7bn, GBP 1.9bn above base) across the commercial and unsecured books, where NatWest is more exposed than a mortgage-led peer. Evelyn Partners integration disappoints (client attrition, no synergies). A bank surcharge or levy increase lifts the tax rate to 27%. Margin troughs at 33.7% and recovers to 35.7% (34.3% ex-SBC): terminal RoTE about 13-14%, a thin spread over CoE. Retention is held at 0 in years 2-3 rather than negative (buybacks pause, CET1 is not released).

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 (Jul-26 to Jun-27) is +7.5% on TTM income of 17,518. FY26 guidance (raised 31 July 2026) is income ex-notables of about GBP 17.9bn including about GBP 275m from Evelyn Partners for H2-26, i.e. +7.6% on FY25; H1-26 income was +11% y/y and NII +12.6% as the structural hedge reprices (+GBP 1.5bn hedge income in 2026 and a further +GBP 1.0bn in 2027, NWG.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:5160-5170). Year 2 (+4.5%) carries the 2027 hedge step and Evelyn's first full year against BoE cuts (guidance assumes 3.75% base rate). Thereafter the customer-balance target (>4% CAL CAGR to 2028) is diluted by deposit and mortgage price competition, fading to 2.5% GBP nominal by year 7.
base.margin_rationale: TTM 'ebitda' margin (PBT + SBC - AT1 - NCI) was 47.8% and H1-26 was 48.5%, with impairment at 19bps. Year 1 at 48.2% is consistent with FY26 guidance: opex ex-litigation about GBP 8.5bn (cost:income about 46%), loan impairment rate <25bps, RoTE >19%. It implies attributable profit of about GBP 6.3bn, RoTE of about 21% on GBP 29-30bn TNAV. Margins hold for a year as hedge income compounds, then fade as impairment normalises to about 30bps through the cycle (about GBP 1.4bn against 19bps today), deposit margins compress with lower rates, and cost growth (pay, technology, Evelyn) runs ahead of a slower income line. Terminal 37.7% (36.3% ex-SBC) gives year-10 attributable profit of about GBP 6.7bn on TNAV of about GBP 40bn, a terminal RoTE of about 16.5%, a 6pt spread over the 10.5% CoE. Management's 2028 >18% RoTE and <45% cost:income targets are deliberately NOT adopted in the base beyond year 2; sustaining them is the bull path.
base.capex_rationale: CET1 retention = 1.480 x g/(1+g), which holds CET1 at the 13.0% target as RWA grows with income.
base.tax_rationale: UK 25% plus 3% bank surcharge; NatWest's reported ETR runs below the 28% headline (24.3% FY25, 26.4% H1-26). TTM on PBT after AT1 coupons 25.9%, held at 26.0%.

bull.margin_rationale: Management's 2028 plan lands and holds: the structural hedge locks in higher yields for longer, CAL grows >4% a year with mortgage share gains (GBP 10bn first-time-buyer commitment), C&I lending keeps compounding at high single digits, Evelyn Partners delivers its synergies and doubles the capital-light wealth fee line, and cost:income moves below 45% by 2028 (Retail toward 40%) on the AI and platform-simplification programme. Impairment stays near 20bps. Terminal RoTE is about 20%, in line with the 2028 >18% target and today's 19.7%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 20%, and bull cut from 35% to 30%, matching the LLOY.L / LYG weighting of its closest peer. NatWest is a pure UK-domestic bank, so its whole book is exposed to one economy and one rate cycle, and Commercial & Institutional (53% of income) carries more cyclical credit than a mortgage book. The shares already price in strong delivery (1.79x reported TNAV at 359p, up from about 1.1x two years ago, after the government exit and three guidance raises). Against that, guidance has been raised rather than cut, NatWest has no material motor-finance exposure, and CET1 is at target with Basel 3.1 quantified, so the bear is not lifted to BCS/HSBA.L's 25%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
